video.title: How To Make Money by Building Simple Apps for Businesses (AI + No-Code)

summary: Chris Koerner and Brandon Doyle each vibe-code a lawn care instant-quote web app in the Emergent tool in under an hour, for about $10 of credits. Brandon builds a polished landing page with lawn size, services and frequency discounts; Chris builds a lead-capture form with lot math, scaled discounts, minimums and a Stripe link, meant to be sent via missed-call text-back. They argue that cheap custom tools beat paying for bloated SaaS like Jobber or Salesforce and can be a free lead magnet into home service businesses. Key takeaway: plain prompts are enough; instant pricing plus speed-to-lead is a competitive edge for trades.

ideas.name: Instant-quote calculator web app for lawn care businesses

tactics.name: Lawn quote pricing logic
steps: Acre = ~43,500 sq ft; subtract house footprint and 10% of lot for driveway
Multiply net sq ft by 1.6 cents (~$45-50 for a 0.1 acre lot)
Discount 20% per quarter acre for big lots

quote.text: I just said multiply the the square footage by 1.6 cents because that's about how you get to about 40 50 bucks
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Speed-to-lead follow-up
steps: Get a text (not just email) for each form submission
Offer a small discount to start this week (quote $80 -> $75)

quote.text: the quote says it would be 80 bucks uh a week, but actually if if we start this week, I'll do it for 75
quote.speaker: Brandon Doyle

tactics.name: Vibe coding without prompt engineering
steps: Write a short plain prompt; include your math example
Ask the same chat how to deploy
Reference a known design (Airbnb style) for good UI
Skip integrations (Google Sheets over SendGrid) to launch fast

quote.text: Like don't get hung up on how perfect your prompt needs to be
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Decide lead-capture friction
steps: Ask for name and phone before showing price for more qualified leads
Or show price first for more volume and fewer contacts

quote.text: The more friction you implement, the fewer leads you get, but the higher quality those leads will be
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: AI-built calculators can output absurd prices ($0, $2,450 per acre); test edge cases and add minimums.

quote.text: one of the quotes it gave me was $0. And the math was right
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Showing price before capturing contact loses leads who dislike the price.

quote.text: if they if they don't like the price, you're never going to get their number, right?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Small businesses pay for bloated SaaS while using a few features; cheap custom tools are an opening.

quote.text: the vast majority of businesses might need like really need three of Jobers 50 features 100 features
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Free niche tools can be a foot in the door to sell bigger services.
Transparent upfront pricing plus speed of reply makes a small trade look like a national brand.

quote.text: transparency of pricing upfront and speed to reply. In the home services industry, those two things are not that normal
quote.speaker: Brandon Doyle

lessons.lesson: Non-coders can ship a working app in under an hour for about $10.
Use the building agent itself as support (how do I deploy?) instead of Googling.

quote.text: just use the chat interface that you're currently using to build the app to ask it questions about the app
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Every question added to a form trades response rate for accuracy.
